Correctly Report LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluations
text: Inputs: p: proportion judged “correct” test set, Pr(Predict = correct) q0: specificity, Pr(Predict = incorrect | True = incorrect) q1: sensitivity, Pr(Predict = correct | True = correct) n: test set size; m0, m1: calibration subset sizes truly incorrect / truly correct items judge must better random (q0 + q1 > 1). Differences Python package, following R conventions: functions vectorised: arguments recycled (length 1 common length), can evaluate many scenarios . Tuples returned data frames named columns (one row per input). Integer arguments (n, m0, m1, m, m_pilot) accept whole number, e.g. 200 well 200L. Invalid input raises R error message Python assertion; q0 + q1 == 1 raises error instead ZeroDivisionError.
